annotations.description: Casting Stormchaser's Talent on Turn 4 before playing the Steam Vents from hand is a sequencing error. The player should play Steam Vents first (it would enter untapped since they control only 3 other lands, wait - Steam Vents always can enter untapped by paying 2 life). More importantly, they should play the land first to have more mana available. Additionally, casting Stormchaser's Talent main phase creates a 1/1 prowess Otter, but casting Sleight of Hand first would be better sequencing - it digs for more cards and triggers prowess on the Otter if cast after Talent. The optimal line is: play Steam Vents (paying 2 life), cast Stormchaser's Talent (creating Otter), then cast Sleight of Hand and/or Opt to trigger prowess before combat. By not playing the land first, they miss the opportunity to have 5 mana available for additional spells this turn.

annotations.description: With Sleight of Hand on the stack and 1 untapped blue mana remaining, casting Opt in response would let them scry away an unwanted card, draw a card, and then have Sleight of Hand look at potentially better top 2 cards. This maximizes card selection depth. Additionally, the Otter token with prowess is on board, so casting Opt during main phase before combat still triggers prowess for a potential attack.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast any spell in response to their own Sleight of Hand.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Opt in response to Sleight of Hand to scry 1 + draw 1 first, improving the quality of cards seen by Sleight of Hand, while also triggering prowess on the Otter token before combat.

annotations.description: Gem3P Proud has an Otter token with prowess on the battlefield and the opponent has no blockers (only lands). They skipped casting any spells precombat and then skipped the attack. They should have attacked with the Otter (1/1 prowess) for at least 1 damage, and ideally cast a spell like Opt before combat to trigger prowess and attack for 2. They also have a Steam Vents in hand they could play to have more mana available. Skipping the attack with an unblockable creature is free damage wasted.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast no spells precombat and then skipped the attack phase entirely, dealing 0 damage with an unblocked Otter token.
annotations.betterLine: Play Steam Vents (paying 2 life or tapped), cast Opt to trigger prowess on the Otter, then attack with the 2/2 Otter for 2 damage. Even without casting a spell, attacking for 1 with the Otter is strictly better than not attacking.

annotations.description: During the combat phase (likely the opponent's end step or during combat), Gem3P Proud declined to cast Opt with open mana. With Riverpyre Verge untapped and an Otter token with prowess on board, casting Opt would have been a free way to dig through the deck and trigger prowess on the Otter if it was attacking. Even outside of combat, casting Opt at end of opponent's turn is almost always correct when you have the mana available and nothing better to do, as it's a pure card selection advantage with no downside.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast any instant during combat/priority window, passing with 1 untapped mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Opt using the untapped Riverpyre Verge to scry 1 and draw a card, gaining card selection advantage at no meaningful cost.

annotations.description: With only Riverpyre Verge untapped and Steam Vents in hand, the player passed without casting Opt at end of turn (or here in postcombat main). They have an Otter token with prowess that could benefit from casting instants, and Opt is a pure cantrip that replaces itself while triggering prowess. Additionally, they could play Steam Vents from hand (paying 2 life or tapped) to have more mana available. Not casting Opt with available mana wastes a prowess trigger opportunity and delays card filtering. However, since they only have one untapped land (Riverpyre Verge), they can cast exactly one spell - Opt would be the best use since it's a cantrip that digs deeper and triggers prowess on the Otter for a slightly bigger attack next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting any spell in postcombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Opt using the untapped Riverpyre Verge to trigger prowess on the Otter token and dig through the library. Could also play Steam Vents from hand first to potentially cast an additional spell.

annotations.description: GPT5n Contra spent all 3 available mana on Three Steps Ahead (draw 2, discard 1) when they could have played a Plains from hand and cast Pinnacle Starcage ({1}{W}{W}) to exile the opponent's Otter token (MV 0) and Stormchaser's Talent is not a creature/artifact so it stays, but the Otter gets exiled. Drawing cards with a 7-card hand that already contains the answer to the opponent's board threat is a misuse of resources.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Three Steps Ahead with mode 3 (draw 2, discard 1) spending all mana on turn 4 main phase
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains, then cast Pinnacle Starcage to exile the opponent's Otter token and any other low-MV creatures/artifacts, neutralizing the opponent's board threat immediately

annotations.description: Discarding Floodfarm Verge when the hand contains duplicate United Battlefronts and other cards that could be discarded instead. Floodfarm Verge is a dual land that provides both W and U mana, which is valuable for casting the various spells in hand (Day of Judgment needs WW, Three Steps Ahead needs U, Pinnacle Starcage needs WW). The player already has 3 lands on board and needs to hit land drops to cast 4-mana spells. While they have Plains and Island in hand, Floodfarm Verge offers more flexibility. A duplicate United Battlefront would have been a better discard since they already have one and may not have time to cast both in a game where they're under pressure from an Otter token and Stormchaser's Talent.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Floodfarm Verge to Three Steps Ahead's draw-two-discard-one mode.
annotations.betterLine: Discard a duplicate United Battlefront, as having two copies of a 4-mana sorcery is less valuable than the mana flexibility Floodfarm Verge provides for casting Day of Judgment and Pinnacle Starcage on time.

annotations.description: During the combat step (before declaring attackers or after), Gem3P had an untapped Riverpyre Verge and one mana available. They could have cast Opt at instant speed to dig for more cards or find relevant spells, using mana that would otherwise go to waste this turn. Declining to use Opt here with available mana is a missed opportunity, though the mana situation is tight (only 1 untapped land). However, the bigger miss is not casting Burst Lightning at the opponent's face or at end of opponent's turn - but since this is their own combat step and they have an Otter to attack with, the main consideration is whether to use the one available mana for Opt before attacks to potentially find something useful. This is a relatively minor missed opportunity for card selection.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast any instant during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Opt with the untapped Riverpyre Verge to scry and draw before deciding on attacks, maximizing information and mana efficiency.

annotations.description: Gem3P Proud has an untapped Riverpyre Verge and one mana available, with Opt in hand. At end of turn (or during postcombat main), they should cast Opt to dig deeper into their deck and trigger prowess on the Otter token. Passing without using available mana and a cantrip is leaving value on the table - both the card selection from Opt and the +1/+1 prowess trigger for potential attacks next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells, wasting the available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Opt with the untapped Riverpyre Verge to scry 1, draw a card, and trigger prowess on the Otter token.

annotations.description: With all lands tapped and no mana available this turn, returning Stock Up (3 mana, draws 2 cards) provides significantly more card advantage than Opt (1 mana, scry 1, draw 1) on future turns. While Opt is cheaper, the player already has several cheap spells in hand (Burst Lightning x2, Into the Flood Maw, Boomerang Basics, Opt) and doesn't need another 1-mana cantrip. Stock Up would provide better card selection and card advantage to find more impactful cards. The mana difference (3 vs 1) is relatively small given they'll have 6+ lands soon.
annotations.actionTaken: Returned Opt from graveyard to hand with Stormchaser's Talent level 2 trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Return Stock Up from graveyard to hand, as it provides superior card selection (look at 5, keep 2) and better card advantage for a modest mana investment.

annotations.description: United Battlefront lets you put up to two noncreature, nonland permanents with mana value 3 or less onto the battlefield FOR FREE (no mana cost required - they enter directly from the library). The player selected only one Perilous Snare when they could have selected two. Perilous Snare exiles a nonland permanent an opponent controls when it enters, so putting two onto the battlefield would exile two of the opponent's permanents (likely the Stormchaser's Talent and the Otter Token). The player's reasoning about not having enough mana is completely wrong - United Battlefront puts the cards directly onto the battlefield without paying their mana costs. Missing the second Perilous Snare means missing a free exile effect on an opponent's permanent.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected only one Perilous Snare from United Battlefront's effect, citing incorrect reasoning about insufficient mana.
annotations.betterLine: Select two Perilous Snares to put onto the battlefield for free, exiling two of the opponent's nonland permanents (Stormchaser's Talent and the Otter Token being the prime targets).

annotations.description: Gem3P Proud has a Slickshot Show-Off in hand with an Otter token on board (from Stormchaser's Talent), the opponent is tapped out at 18 life with no blockers, and Gem3P has 5 untapped lands. Casting Slickshot Show-Off (1R) and then following up with cheap noncreature spells like Opt and Burst Lightning would trigger Slickshot's +2/+0 multiple times and Otter's prowess, enabling a massive attack. Instead, they passed without casting anything, wasting a full turn of development and damage when the opponent is completely tapped out with no board presence.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the main phase without casting any spells despite having mana available and the opponent tapped out with no creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Slickshot Show-Off (1R), then cast Opt (U) triggering Slickshot (+2/+0 to 3/2) and Otter prowess (2/2), then cast Burst Lightning (R) targeting opponent for 2 damage, triggering Slickshot again (5/2) and Otter prowess again (3/3). Attack with Slickshot (5/2 flying haste) and Otter (3/3) for 8 damage plus 2 from Burst Lightning = 10 damage, putting opponent to 8.

annotations.description: The player is in the combat phase with an Otter Token (1/1 with prowess) attacking. They cast Opt during combat, which triggers prowess (+1/+1), but they missed the opportunity to cast Wild Ride on the Otter during their main phase before combat. Wild Ride ({R}, sorcery) would have given the Otter +3/+0, and as a noncreature spell would trigger prowess for an additional +1/+1. Combined with other cheap spells like Opt and Burst Lightning to the face, they could have dealt significantly more damage this turn. The player's own reasoning acknowledges they missed the main phase window for Wild Ride, which is a sorcery that had to be cast pre-combat. With Wild Ride + Opt during main phase, the Otter would have been at least 1+3+1+1 = 6 power before combat, plus additional spells during combat could pump further.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Opt during combat phase, getting only +1/+1 prowess trigger on the Otter Token, dealing 2 damage with the Otter.
annotations.betterLine: During the first main phase, cast Wild Ride targeting Otter Token (+3/+0 and haste, plus prowess trigger for +1/+1), making it a 5/2. Then attack, and during combat cast Opt and potentially Burst Lightning to the opponent's face for massive damage. The Otter alone could have dealt 5+ damage instead of 2, plus 2-4 from Burst Lightning.

annotations.description: With an Otter Token (prowess) attacking and Opt on the stack, casting Burst Lightning targeting the opponent would trigger prowess on the Otter for +1/+1, dealing 1 extra combat damage. The opponent has all lands tapped and no creatures, so there's no strategic reason to hold Burst Lightning. Missing 1 damage matters in an aggro/tempo deck.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast Burst Lightning during combat, missing a prowess trigger on the attacking Otter Token.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Burst Lightning targeting the opponent to get an additional prowess trigger on the Otter, dealing 1 extra combat damage (total ~5 damage this turn instead of ~4).

annotations.description: During combat, Gem3P Proud cast Burst Lightning targeting the opponent's face for 2 damage rather than holding it. The Otter Token is already tapped and attacking, so the Burst Lightning triggers prowess giving the Otter +1/+1 (making it 2/2), which adds 1 extra damage. However, the total output is 2 (burn) + 2 (Otter with prowess) = 4 damage. If instead they had cast Wild Ride targeting the Otter (+3/+0, making it a 4/1 with prowess triggering to 5/2), they'd deal 5 damage from the Otter alone, and could save the Burst Lightning for later (either as removal or face damage). The Wild Ride line deals 5 damage this turn while preserving Burst Lightning, versus 4 damage while spending both a burn spell. That said, casting Burst Lightning now to apply pressure and trigger prowess is a reasonable aggro line, and saving Wild Ride for a future Slickshot Show-Off turn could also be valid. The sequencing is debatable but likely slightly worse.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Burst Lightning targeting GPT5n Contra (opponent's face) for 2 damage during combat, triggering Otter prowess for +1/+1.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Wild Ride targeting the attacking Otter Token for +3/+0, triggering prowess for +1/+1, dealing 5 combat damage total while preserving Burst Lightning for future use as removal or burn.

annotations.description: The player chose to Plot Slickshot Show-Off (exiling it to cast for free next turn), but the game log shows it was actually cast and put onto the battlefield instead. Looking at the board state: opponent is at 9 life with all lands tapped, and Gem3P has an Otter token that already attacked this turn. With Slickshot Show-Off having haste, plotting it is reasonable to combine it with spells next turn for a big attack. However, the opponent is at 9 life with no board presence and all lands tapped. Casting Slickshot now puts a 1/2 flyer on the board that can attack next turn regardless, and plotting delays the pressure by a turn while telegraphing the threat. More importantly, with Wild Ride in hand (+3/+0), casting the Show-Off now means next turn you can attack with both the Otter and Show-Off, cast Wild Ride on Show-Off (triggering prowess twice - once for Wild Ride, once for Show-Off's ability), making it potentially a 8/2 flyer (1+2+2+3=8) plus the Otter attacking with prowess. Plotting doesn't gain much here since the opponent has no mana up for countermagic and no creatures to threaten. The difference is marginal though - plotting does mean the cast next turn is 'free' allowing more spells to be chained.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to Plot Slickshot Show-Off for {1}{R}
annotations.betterLine: Cast Slickshot Show-Off normally to put it on the battlefield immediately, preserving the option to attack next turn with both creatures and chain spells for maximum prowess/pump damage, potentially threatening lethal with Wild Ride.

annotations.description: GPT5n Contra is at 9 life facing a Stormchaser's Talent (which creates prowess Otter tokens) and an Otter token already on board, with the opponent having a graveyard full of cheap instants/sorceries. A Simulacrum Synthesizer is on the stack - this is an artifact, not a critical threat. Meanwhile, GPT5n Contra chose to use Three Steps Ahead to draw 2 cards and discard 1 (paying {1}{U} + {2} = 3U total) instead of countering the Simulacrum Synthesizer ({1}{U} + {1}{U} = 2UU total). However, looking more carefully at the board state, the Synthesizer generates construct tokens when artifacts with MV 3+ enter - in the opponent's UR spells deck this is unlikely to be the primary threat. The real issue is that at 9 life with all lands tapped, they should be countering the Simulacrum Synthesizer rather than drawing cards. The Synthesizer will generate growing construct tokens that compound the board pressure. At 9 life, every threat matters, and GPT5n Contra has Day of Judgment and Pinnacle Starcage in hand already - they don't need to dig for answers, they need to survive. Countering the Synthesizer would cost the same mana and prevent future token generation.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to draw 2 cards and discard 1 with Three Steps Ahead instead of countering Simulacrum Synthesizer on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Counter the Simulacrum Synthesizer with Three Steps Ahead. At 9 life, preventing an engine that creates growing construct tokens is more important than drawing cards, especially when already holding Day of Judgment and Pinnacle Starcage as answers.

annotations.description: GPT5n Contra already has Day of Judgment in hand, making a second copy on top redundant. Hide on the Ceiling offers unique instant-speed interaction that could be more valuable for surviving burst prowess/burn turns at 9 life against Izzet aggro.
annotations.actionTaken: Bottomed Hide on the Ceiling, keeping Day of Judgment on top (already had Day of Judgment in hand)
annotations.betterLine: Bottom Day of Judgment instead, keeping Hide on the Ceiling on top for instant-speed flexibility since Day of Judgment is already in hand

annotations.description: At 9 life against an aggressive prowess/burn deck, GPT5n Contra chose to draw 2 cards instead of countering Slickshot Show-Off, which is a flying haste creature that grows +2/+0 per noncreature spell. The opponent has already shown multiple burn spells (2x Burst Lightning, Shock on stack) and prowess creatures. Slickshot Show-Off will deal massive damage with the opponent's spell-heavy game plan, and at 9 life there's very little margin for error.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose 'Draw two cards, then discard a card' mode for Three Steps Ahead
annotations.betterLine: Choose 'Counter target spell' mode to counter Slickshot Show-Off, removing the most dangerous threat on the stack. A flying haste creature that scales with noncreature spells is devastating against a control deck at 9 life.

annotations.description: GPT5n Contra is at 9 life facing a Slickshot Show-Off (a 1/2 flyer with haste that gets +2/+0 per noncreature spell cast) plus an Otter token with prowess, and there's a Shock on the stack. The stack contains Three Steps Ahead (which GPT5n is currently resolving), an Otter Token being created, Slickshot Show-Off, and Shock. By choosing 'Done' with only the copy mode selected, GPT5n is NOT countering any of these threatening spells. The Slickshot Show-Off is extremely dangerous - with Stormchaser's Talent potentially at level 3 creating more tokens, and each noncreature spell pumping it. At 9 life, letting Slickshot resolve along with Shock (2 damage) is very dangerous. GPT5n should have also selected the counter mode to counter either Slickshot Show-Off or Shock from the stack.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected only the copy mode for Three Steps Ahead (creating a token copy of an artifact/creature) without also selecting the counter mode to stop a threatening spell on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Should have selected both the counter mode (to counter Slickshot Show-Off, which is the most dangerous threat on the stack) and potentially the copy mode as well, paying the additional costs. At minimum, countering Slickshot Show-Off would prevent a major source of damage.

annotations.description: Gem3P Proud is at 18 life with the opponent at 7 life. They have an Otter Token (1/1 with prowess) and Stormchaser's Talent on the battlefield. The opponent has Simulacrum Synthesizer but no creatures to block. It appears the player missed attacking with the Otter Token during combat this turn, and now in postcombat main they're casting Wild Ride on the Otter Token which accomplishes very little — it gives +3/+0 and haste to a creature that already has haste (from prowess triggering) but can no longer attack since combat is over. Wild Ride's +3/+0 and haste are useless postcombat. Additionally, with the opponent at 7 life, they had Into the Flood Maw and Boomerang Basics available. Into the Flood Maw could bounce the Simulacrum Synthesizer (the opponent's only meaningful permanent), and the burn spells already in the graveyard suggest an aggressive strategy. Casting Wild Ride postcombat wastes a card for zero impact.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Wild Ride targeting Otter Token in postcombat main, giving it +3/+0 and haste when it can no longer attack.
annotations.betterLine: Should have attacked with the Otter Token during combat (it appears combat was missed/skipped). In postcombat main, should have cast Into the Flood Maw to bounce the Simulacrum Synthesizer, removing the opponent's key artifact and clearing the way for future attacks. Wild Ride postcombat is a complete waste of a card.

annotations.description: Bouncing Simulacrum Synthesizer doesn't draw a card since it's an opponent's permanent. With the opponent at 7 life, bouncing own Stormchaser's Talent would draw a card (potentially finding burn for lethal) and could be replayed next turn to create another Otter token. The Synthesizer has no creatures to generate yet and Into the Flood Maw in hand could handle it later if needed.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Simulacrum Synthesizer with Boomerang Basics, returning opponent's artifact without drawing a card
annotations.betterLine: Target own Stormchaser's Talent to draw a card, potentially finding burn to close out the game at 7 life, then replay Talent next turn for another Otter

annotations.description: GPT5n Contra is at 7 life facing a Stormchaser's Talent with an Otter token (prowess creature) on the opponent's board, with the opponent having a graveyard full of cheap spells. Instead of casting a meaningful spell, they cast Hide on the Ceiling with X=0, which exiles zero targets and accomplishes literally nothing — it's a completely wasted card. They have Day of Judgment in hand which would clear the Otter, or could cast Pinnacle Starcage (which would exile the Otter since it has MV ≤ 2), or Simulacrum Synthesizer to start building a board. At 7 life against a prowess/burn deck with Burst Lightning, Shock, and Wild Ride already in the graveyard (and Stormchaser's Talent potentially recovering spells at level 2), every card matters enormously.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Hide on the Ceiling with X=0, targeting nothing, wasting a card and mana for zero effect.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Day of Judgment to destroy the Otter token, or cast Pinnacle Starcage to exile the Otter (MV ≤ 2) and any other small threats. At minimum, cast Simulacrum Synthesizer to develop the board. Any of these lines would be vastly superior to a zero-target Hide on the Ceiling.

annotations.description: GPT5n Contra is at 7 life facing an Otter token with prowess and a Stormchaser's Talent that could generate more threats. They're scrying 2 from Simulacrum Synthesizer entering the battlefield. They chose to bottom Simulacrum Synthesizer and keep Hide on the Ceiling on top. Given that they already have a Simulacrum Synthesizer on the battlefield and their hand contains Day of Judgment (which they desperately need to cast to survive), keeping Hide on the Ceiling is defensible as a tempo play, but a second Synthesizer could generate significant value with their artifact-heavy hand (Pinnacle Starcage, Repurposing Bay). However, at 7 life with all lands tapped, the priority is survival - Day of Judgment is already in hand, and Hide on the Ceiling could serve as emergency interaction if needed before they can cast Day of Judgment next turn. The decision is reasonable but debatable - the second Synthesizer could have been valuable for the longer game plan.
annotations.actionTaken: Bottomed Simulacrum Synthesizer and kept Hide on the Ceiling on top during scry 2
annotations.betterLine: This is close - keeping Hide on the Ceiling for potential emergency interaction at 7 life is defensible, but a second Simulacrum Synthesizer would synergize well with the artifacts in hand (Pinnacle Starcage, Repurposing Bay) for the mid-game plan after stabilizing with Day of Judgment.

annotations.description: Into the Flood Maw can only target permanents an opponent controls, not your own. The player attempted to target their own Stormchaser's Talent, which is an illegal target. The reasoning about triggering prowess on multiple Slickshots is also flawed — no Slickshot Show-Offs are visible on the battlefield. With opponent at 7 life and all lands tapped, the correct line would be to target the opponent's Simulacrum Synthesizer with Into the Flood Maw (removing their artifact) and attack with the Otter, or cast Wild Ride from graveyard on the Otter for +3/+0 to push more damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Into the Flood Maw targeting own Stormchaser's Talent, based on a confused plan involving nonexistent Slickshot Show-Offs on the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Into the Flood Maw targeting opponent's Simulacrum Synthesizer to remove their artifact, then attack with Otter Token. Or if Slickshots were plotted and about to be cast, sequence spells to maximize prowess triggers after combat.
